nodes.name: Kart rigid body
nodes.purpose: Per-update rigid body step for every kart: force accumulation, drag, speed length limit, angular integration and pose composition

nodes.name: Wheel suspension
nodes.purpose: Four spring-damper wheel struts that hold the body above the ground, measure travel against the collision result and ease the tyre radius down on sink surfaces

nodes.name: Kart surface response
nodes.purpose: Reads field collision attributes into kart surface state and applies the resulting wrench: floor type, boost pads, jump pads, halfpipe ramps, walls and body hitboxes

nodes.name: Course mesh collision
nodes.purpose: Packed attribute prisms, the block tree that indexes them, point and sphere narrow phase, and the cached repeat queries every kart part goes through

nodes.name: Object and drivable collision
nodes.purpose: Collision against course objects and movable drivable props, each with its own local mesh, placement matrix and spatial cache

nodes.name: CPU driver
nodes.purpose: CPU path following around a bump: alignment of the impact with the body forward axis, a scaled backward path offset, and trick requests while airborne

cards.name: Force to velocity integration
cards.summary: One routine sums forces into an external velocity, damps it, and builds the displacement vector for the update.
cards.behavior: One routine moves the body each update. It takes a time step, a top speed and an airborne flag from the caller. The routine does not fix the time step. The summed force becomes acceleration with no mass division. The external velocity gains acceleration times the time step. The gravity term is added to the force sum only when the body flag named noGravity is true. That flag is false after setup, so this routine adds no gravity in the default state. The source of gravity is not visible in this tree. When the hit flag is set and the length of the previous displacement is above zero, the vertical part of the external velocity becomes zero. A second flag clears the vertical part with no condition. The external velocity is then multiplied by 0.998 once per call. The displacement is the external velocity times the time step plus the internal, moving-road and moving-water velocities. A separate forward-speed value is the length of the horizontal external velocity projected on the body axis, times a dot product of two body axes. Its sign flips whenever a second dot product is not exactly zero, so it is not a clean forward or reverse test. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: external velocity drag
constants.unit: multiplier on the external velocity, applied once per call of the step routine

constants.name: vertical external velocity while hit
constants.unit: value written to the vertical external velocity when the hit flag is set and the previous displacement length is above zero

constants.name: default gravity force term
constants.unit: default value of the gravity field; the routine adds it only when the noGravity flag is true, and that flag defaults to false

cards.name: Top speed clamp and airborne cap
cards.summary: The displacement is split into a unit direction and a length. Only the stored length is limited to the top speed.
cards.behavior: After the displacement is built, the routine splits it into a unit direction and a length. The length goes into a speed-norm field. When the model scale on the z axis is below 1, the top speed from the caller is first multiplied by that scale. When the length is above the top speed, the stored length is set to the top speed. Only the stored length is limited. The position then advances by the direction vector, which is a unit vector at that point. As written here, the position step is therefore one unit per call. The shipped game may scale this step by the limited length, and this tree does not show it. A separate cut applies when the airborne flag is set. A vertical internal velocity above 120 is set to 120. The lower side is not cut. The kart physics object copies the direction vector for other code to read. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: airborne vertical internal velocity cap
constants.unit: upper limit on the vertical internal velocity, applied each call while the airborne flag is set; time base unverified

constants.name: model scale threshold for the top speed
constants.unit: top speed is multiplied by the z scale only when that scale is below this value

cards.name: Angular motion and upright limits
cards.summary: Angular velocity is damped, limited per axis and integrated into the orientation quaternion each update.
cards.behavior: The routine first multiplies the main angular velocity by 0.98. It then adds the torque response. The source comment calls this part odd. The response is the inverse inertia times the torque times the time step, averaged with a second term that repeats the inverse inertia on that result plus the torque. The routine then calls an upright hook when the upright flag is set. The base body does nothing there. The bike body sets the z component of the angular velocity to zero. Next the x and y components are limited to plus or minus 0.4 and the z component to plus or minus 0.8. The y component is then multiplied by a yaw factor that is 0.0 after setup, so the main angular velocity gives no yaw unless other code changes that factor. The total angular velocity is the sum of two other angular velocities and the main one times a per-vehicle factor. The quaternion gains the product of itself and the total, times the time step, times 0.5. The quaternion is normalised and falls back to identity when it is near zero. A stabilise hook runs next when the upright flag is set. Its body is not in this tree. The final orientation is the main, extra and special rotations multiplied in that order. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: angular velocity damping
constants.unit: multiplier on the main angular velocity, applied once per call of the step routine

constants.name: first axis angular clamp
constants.unit: limit on the x component, plus and minus, applied each call; the unit assumes the time step scaling in the quaternion update

constants.name: second axis angular clamp
constants.unit: limit on the y component, plus and minus, applied each call before the yaw factor

constants.name: third axis angular clamp
constants.unit: limit on the z component, plus and minus, applied each call

constants.name: torque response weight
constants.unit: weight on the two-term torque response, applied once per call

constants.name: default yaw factor
constants.unit: default of the multiplier on the y component of the main angular velocity; other code may set it

constants.name: stored stabilisation factor
constants.unit: default of a field for the stabilise hook; the hook body is not in this tree

cards.name: Box inertia tensor
cards.summary: Setup builds a diagonal inertia tensor with unit mass from two vectors and stores its inverse.
cards.behavior: Setup takes two vectors and builds a diagonal inertia tensor. Each diagonal term is a twelfth of the squares of the other two components of the first vector, plus the squares of the same two components of the second vector. There is no mass term, so the mass is one. The first vector acts like the box size and the second like an offset, but the names are not given. The inverse is computed once and stored. Later steps multiply the torque by this inverse and need no division. A vehicle can skip this setup, and the tensor then stays the identity. The same inverse feeds an angular-acceleration helper. The angular velocity factor is stored from the same setup call, and its default of 1.0 is replaced by the per-vehicle value. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: box inertia divisor
constants.unit: divisor for the first vector, applied once at setup

constants.name: default angular velocity factor
constants.unit: default multiplier on the main angular velocity; the per-vehicle setup call overwrites it

cards.name: Spring-damper suspension strut
cards.summary: Each strut turns travel and travel speed into a spring-damper force and applies it at the suspension top while a floor is held.
cards.behavior: Travel is measured along the strut down direction between the wheel and the suspension top, with a minimum of zero. The work runs only when the wheel reports a floor. The raw force is minus the spring stiffness times the missing travel, plus the damping factor times the travel speed. It points along the down direction. During respawn its vertical part is limited to plus or minus 1. The horizontal part of the force is projected on the floor normal, and the vertical result is added to the vertical force. The vertical force is then limited to the maximum vertical acceleration from the kart stats. It becomes zero when the external vertical velocity is above 5, or when a flag turns off the vertical suspension force. The body gets only the vertical part of this force. The torque comes from the raw force at the suspension top. Its x part is dropped during a wheelie, and its y part is always dropped. Unless a bullet flag is set, the strut then applies a floor moment. A speed-shaping branch needs a counter above zero, and nothing in this tree sets that counter above zero. That branch does not run here. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: vertical external velocity that disables the force
constants.unit: compared with the body external vertical velocity each update; time base unverified

constants.name: respawn vertical force limit
constants.unit: plus and minus limit on the vertical part of the raw force while the respawn state is active

cards.name: Wheel travel limits and tyre squash
cards.summary: Wheel travel is clamped between zero and the scaled strut maximum, and the tyre radius eases toward a sink-reduced target.
cards.behavior: Travel is the distance along the strut down direction from the suspension top to the wheel. The update clamps it to the strut maximum times the vertical scale, with a minimum of zero. The wheel position is rebuilt from that travel. The wheel velocity is the position change minus the internal, moving-road and moving-water velocities and two collision movements. A separate collision-state call lets the stored travel grow by at most 5 times the vertical scale per update before it is limited to the new maximum. In the collision pass, a wheel that reports a floor or wall contact moves out along the contact offset. The target radius becomes the wheel radius minus a sink amount. The amount is a global sink factor times the surface sink depth, stored as an integer. The factor value is not in this tree. The radius moves 0.1 of the way to the target each update. When the measured travel is below zero, the pass sets a suspension-limit flag and reports the overshoot to the physics engine. That pass keeps the negative value as the travel. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: tyre radius easing
constants.unit: fraction of the gap to the target radius closed per update

constants.name: travel growth allowance
constants.unit: world units times the vertical scale, added to the stored travel before the clamp in the collision-state call

constants.name: minimum wheel travel
constants.unit: floor for the travel in the wheel update, applied each update

cards.name: Wheel probe sphere and scrub
cards.summary: Each wheel probes the course with one sphere placed slightly ahead of the wheel, and applies a floor moment with a lower lateral rate during wall scraping.
cards.behavior: Each wheel owns one collision sphere, created with a radius of 10 and scaled by the kart scale. The collision call also gets the wheel radius from the vehicle data, so the source does not show which radius the solver uses. The probe center sits at the wheel position, moved along the down direction by the difference between the current and the nominal tyre radius. It is then moved forward along the body by 0.3 times the wheel radius times the lean and the total scale. The probe movement vector is the gravity argument times the time step times 10. It is not the kart velocity. The probe is skipped in several states, for example a halfpipe midair state and the cannon state. While the wheel holds a floor, the strut applies a floor moment unless a bullet flag is set. The forward rate is 0.1. The lateral rate is 0.01 while a wall-contact flag is set and 0.8 otherwise. The last argument of the moment call is false during a large flip hit or a wheelie. Its meaning is not named here. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: wheel probe sphere radius
constants.unit: radius given when the wheel sphere is created, scaled by the hitbox scale; the collision call also receives the wheel radius

constants.name: probe forward offset factor
constants.unit: multiplier on wheel radius, lean and total scale, applied each update

constants.name: probe movement factor
constants.unit: multiplier on the time step and the gravity argument, set each update

constants.name: floor moment forward rate
constants.unit: forward rate passed to the floor moment call

constants.name: wall-scrape lateral rate
constants.unit: lateral rate passed to the floor moment call while the wall-contact flag is set

constants.name: default lateral rate
constants.unit: lateral rate otherwise; the field is set at collision init and not changed in this tree

constants.name: wheel hitbox start height
constants.unit: world units above the body position, used as the previous position of the wheel hitbox at setup

cards.name: Floor attribute classification
cards.summary: The attribute word of the nearest floor prism sets the surface type, a variant, a sink depth and three behavior bits.
cards.behavior: Each collision prism stores one 16-bit attribute word. Bits 0 to 4 hold the surface type. Bits 5 to 7 hold a variant. Bits 11 and 12 hold a sink depth step. Bit 13 marks a trickable surface, bit 14 a road-reject surface, and bit 15 a soft wall. The floor pass reads the nearest floor entry. It copies the sink depth and keeps the lowest speed factor seen in that collision record. It adds the handling factor for the surface type. The factors come from per-vehicle tables that are not in this tree. Bit 14 sets a reject-road kart flag. Bit 13 sets the trickable flag, and otherwise a not-trickable surface marker is set. The pass also keeps the floor type mask and variant. Offroad, moving road and sticky road each set their own marker or kart flag. The soft-wall bit is read only in the wall pass, where it sets a soft-wall flag on the contact. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: attribute type field mask
constants.unit: bit mask on the attribute word, applied for each prism read

constants.name: attribute variant mask
constants.unit: bit mask applied after a shift of 5

constants.name: sink depth field shift
constants.unit: bit position of the 2-bit sink depth field

constants.name: trickable attribute bit
constants.unit: bit mask, tested for each floor contact

constants.name: road reject attribute bit
constants.unit: bit mask, tested for each floor contact

constants.name: soft wall attribute bit
constants.unit: bit mask, tested for each wall contact

cards.name: Boost pads and boost ramps
cards.summary: A floor prism of the boost pad type sets a pad bit on wheel contact. A boost ramp sets its own bit and stores its variant.
cards.behavior: Two floor types can start a boost. The first is the flat boost pad. It is checked for wheel contacts only. A body contact does nothing. It sets the boost-panel pad bit and the boost-panel surface marker. The second is the boost ramp. It is checked for any contact. It sets the ramp pad bit, stores the attribute variant as the ramp type, and sets the boost-panel, ramp and trickable surface markers. Without a ramp entry, the stored ramp type is reset to the invalid value and the not-trickable marker is set. The code that turns a pad bit into speed is not in this tree. The pad bits are inputs to later movement code. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: boost panel pad bit
constants.unit: bit mask set for each wheel contact on a boost pad

constants.name: boost ramp pad bit
constants.unit: bit mask set for each contact on a boost ramp

constants.name: boost panel surface marker
constants.unit: bit mask set for each pad or ramp contact

constants.name: boost ramp surface marker
constants.unit: bit mask set for each ramp contact

cards.name: Jump pads and trampolines
cards.summary: A jump-pad floor prism arms a pad launch unless the kart already holds the pad state, and always marks the contact trickable.
cards.behavior: A jump pad is read from the same floor pass as any other floor, for wheel and body contacts. The pad is armed when the kart is not on the ground or not yet flagged as on a jump pad, and the velocity-increase flag is not set. Arming sets the jump-pad bit in the pad mask and stores the attribute variant as the jump pad type. The movement code that makes the launch is not in this tree. The contact is flagged trickable in every case, whether the pad armed or not. A kart that already holds the velocity-increase state is never armed again. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: jump pad floor type index
constants.unit: surface type number in the attribute word

constants.name: jump pad pad bit
constants.unit: bit mask set when a pad arms

cards.name: Halfpipe ramps
cards.summary: A halfpipe-ramp floor prism sets halfpipe flags, a surface marker and a 2-count invisibility timer on the kart.
cards.behavior: A halfpipe ramp has its own floor type. A contact sets the halfpipe-ramp kart flag. It also sets the local variant of that flag unless the kart is an online remote copy. It sets the halfpipe surface marker and sets a halfpipe invisibility timer on the kart state to 2. The code that reads that timer is not in this tree, so its unit is unverified. A prism with variant 1 also sets the boost-panel pad bit. The trickable test for the same floor entry runs earlier in the same pass. It does not depend on the ramp type. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: halfpipe invisibility timer
constants.unit: value written to the kart state for each ramp contact; unit unverified because the reader is not in this tree

constants.name: halfpipe ramp floor type
constants.unit: surface type number in the attribute word

constants.name: halfpipe ramp surface marker
constants.unit: bit mask set for each ramp contact

cards.name: Wall contact and soft-wall bookkeeping
cards.summary: A wall pass reads two masks and records the wall type, variant and soft flag. The floor pass keeps separate soft and non-soft height sums.
cards.behavior: The wall pass asks two masks in order. The first mask finds a wall that takes part in player collision. It reads the type and variant of the closest entry. The second mask must also match before those values are stored on the contact. Only then does the soft-wall attribute bit set the soft-wall flag. In the floor pass, a contact with the soft-wall flag adds one to a soft counter and adds the sphere bottom height to a soft sum. This happens even when no floor entry is found. A floor contact without the flag adds one to a non-soft counter and adds the same height to a non-soft sum. What reads these sums is not in this tree. The kart bounding radius is set at init and is the largest sphere extent times the hitbox scale. The code declares a bump timer and an out-of-bounds timer. This tree only sets both to zero. The ten-frame and three-frame limits appear only in comments. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: initial bounding radius
constants.unit: world units; init replaces it with the hitbox extent times the hitbox scale

cards.name: Body hitbox rig
cards.summary: The body collision shape is a set of up to 16 enabled spheres, re-placed from the current pose each update.
cards.behavior: The vehicle data holds 16 sphere slots. Each slot has an enabled flag, a local position, a radius, a wall-only flag and a tyre index. Only enabled slots make a sphere. Each update every sphere is placed again. The local x and z are multiplied by the body scale. The sink depth is added to the local y, and the sum is multiplied by the y scale. When the y scale is below the total scale, an extra lift of the scale difference times the radius is added after that. The result is rotated by the body orientation and added to the body position. Setting a hitbox scale multiplies every sphere radius. The bounding radius is the largest of three values. Each value is the largest sphere radius plus the absolute local position on one axis. The bounding radius is computed once when the group is built. The same pass returns half of the largest z extent. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: sphere slots in a body rig
constants.unit: slots in the vehicle data; enabled slots become spheres

constants.name: hitbox group default scale
constants.unit: scale before setHitboxScale is called

constants.name: returned depth fraction
constants.unit: fraction of the largest z extent returned at setup

cards.name: Attribute block lookup
cards.summary: A point query walks an octree of 4-byte nodes in the course collision data to find a list of prism indices.
cards.behavior: A point query first subtracts the minimum corner of the tree area from the point and truncates each axis to an integer. A non-zero result after the axis mask means the point is outside the tree, and the lookup returns nothing. Inside, the root index comes from the coordinates shifted by the block width and packed from the three axes. Each node holds a 32-bit word. When the top bit is set, the node is a leaf, and its low 31 bits are a byte offset to the prism index list. Otherwise the word is a byte offset to the next node. The shift is then decremented, and the child index takes one bit from each axis, which gives eight children. A separate pass builds a bounding box over the three vertices of every prism, starting from the 999999 sentinel. Object code uses that box. The tree area check does not use it. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: bounding box sentinel extent
constants.unit: world units, start value for the prism bounding box before the vertex pass

constants.name: leaf marker bit
constants.unit: bit mask in a node word, tested at each level

constants.name: leaf offset mask
constants.unit: bit mask in a leaf word, applied once per lookup

cards.name: Prism point test
cards.summary: A point test checks the point against three edge planes and the face plane of each candidate prism, then filters by thickness and type.
cards.behavior: For each candidate prism, the point test subtracts the stored vertex from the point. It takes the dot product with two edge normals and a third edge normal minus the prism height. A prism is skipped when any of the three is 0.01 or more. The face distance is 0.01 minus the dot product with the face normal. A distance of zero or less skips the prism. A prism is also skipped when the distance reaches the prism thickness plus 0.02. Then the type bit of the prism must match the requested mask. The movement variant runs when the previous position is finite. It also skips a prism of a directional type when the movement has a positive dot product with the face normal. The point-only variant has no such test. A hit returns the distance, the face normal and the attribute word. The iterator stays at that prism so the next call continues. A miss at the end of the list clears the iterator. A sphere test exists with extra edge and corner checks. This card does not cover it. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: edge plane skin distance
constants.unit: world units; a prism is skipped when a plane test is this value or more

constants.name: thickness tolerance
constants.unit: world units added to the prism thickness in the depth test

constants.name: minimum face distance
constants.unit: world units; a face distance at or below this skips the prism

cards.name: Cached collision queries
cards.summary: A narrow-scope call collects colliding prisms into a short list. Cached lookups reuse that list while the query sphere stays inside the stored sphere.
cards.behavior: The cached path depends on a narrow-scope call. That call stores a position and a radius and runs the sphere test on the nearby prisms. It fills a list of up to 0x100 prism indices with the prisms that hit. Cached point and sphere lookups then test whether the new query sphere lies inside the stored sphere. The point lookup uses a query radius of 0.01. On a hit, the lookup sets the iterator to the start of the stored list. It skips the block-tree walk. It copies the new movement and type mask. On a miss, the normal block-tree lookup runs. The sphere miss path limits the radius to the radius the course data declares. The hit path does not. The results of a cached and an uncached query are not proven equal by this tree. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: cached point query radius
constants.unit: world units, radius tested against the stored sphere and assigned on a hit

constants.name: prism list capacity
constants.unit: prism indices, size of the collected list

cards.name: Object and drivable collision layers
cards.summary: Course objects test points in their own local space, and drivable props are visited through a spatial manager.
cards.behavior: A course object owns a collision mesh and a placement matrix. A query is moved into object space with the inverse matrix. The same prism point test runs there with the object scale. The returned bounding box is moved back to world space and merged into the caller result. When the previous position is not finite, the object path uses an infinite vector for the previous position. Drivable props are visited through a box collision manager with a drivable flag. A cached query asks whether the point lies in that manager spatial cache. When it does not, the call falls back to the normal uncached drivable query. When it does, only the drivables in that cache are tested. Their results are combined with a logical or. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: default local mesh scale
constants.unit: scale of an object mesh at construction; setup code may change it

constants.name: drivable cache probe radius
constants.unit: world units, sphere radius used for the point-in-cache test

cards.name: CPU path offset after a bump
cards.summary: A bump handler maps the impact alignment to a negative path offset rate for a computer driver, and always relays the bump to the look-at handler.
cards.behavior: When a computer driver is bumped, the handler takes the dot product of the body forward axis and the bump direction. A positive dot gives a sign of plus 1, and any other value gives minus 1. The absolute dot product is mapped from the window 5 to 15 onto 0 to 1 and clamped. A bump of the same size as a unit vector gives zero. The offset rate runs from minus 500 at zero to minus 650 at one. It is multiplied by the sign and sent to the path handler, which recalculates its target. The handler is called for any driver. Only a computer driver gets the offset. All drivers relay the bump to the look-at handler. The caller is not in this tree, so the length of the bump direction is unknown. If it is a unit vector, the offset rate always stays at minus 500. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: alignment window lower bound
constants.unit: absolute dot product that maps to 0

constants.name: alignment window upper bound
constants.unit: absolute dot product that maps to 1

constants.name: smallest path offset rate
constants.unit: rate at the lower bound; the time base is unverified

constants.name: largest path offset rate
constants.unit: rate at the upper bound; the time base is unverified

cards.name: Lap checkpoint crossing
cards.summary: A sector test passes only when two signed cross values, one per edge of the next checkpoint, are not negative.
cards.behavior: Course data stores a checkpoint as a left and a right point, a lap-check marker, a respawn index and links to the previous and next checkpoints. Each link stores two edge difference vectors. The sector test takes two 2D points from the caller. It computes one signed cross value for the first point with the first edge vector. It computes another for the second point with the second edge vector. The test fails when either value is below zero. A value of exactly zero passes. Each checkpoint also keeps a per-player bit mask. This tree does not show how the mask is set or used for crossing. The code that supplies the two points is not in this tree. This tree is a decompilation, so some names are guesses.

constants.name: first edge side threshold
constants.unit: cross value below this fails the test, applied once per sector test

constants.name: second edge side threshold
constants.unit: cross value below this fails the test, applied once per sector test
